body.p: Claims 1-7 and 13-15 are pending in this application, of which claim 1 is independent. By this amendment, claims 1, 3, 13, and 15 are amended and claim 14 is canceled without prejudice to or disclaimer of the subject matter recited therein. No new matter is added, rather the claims have been amended to comport with US best practice, recasting claims 13 and 15 in independent form.

The Office has rejected claims 1-3, 5-7, and 13-15 under 35 U.S.C. 5 103 as being unpatentable over U.S. Pub. No. 2020/0250406 to Wang, et a. ("Wang"), and U.S. Pub. No. 2015/0005650 to Banet, et al. ("Banet"). Office Action, p. 3. Claim 4 has been rejected as unpatentable over Wang and Banet in further view of U.S. Pub. No. 2017/0238842 to Jacquel, et al. ("Jacquel"). Office Action,p. 4.
Amended independent claim 1 recites:
"A computer-implemented method of updating a patient record in a medical
database, the method comprising:
receiving an image depicting a display screen of a patient monitoring system, wherein
the image depicting the display screen of the patient monitor contains a depiction of displaying at
least one vital signs data value of said patient;
evaluating at least one region of interest of said image comprising one of said
vital signs data values to extract said one vital signs data value from said image;
updating the patient record with the extracted at least one vital signs data value; and storing the image in a database such that the image is associated with the
updated patient record." (emphasis added).

Amended independent claims 13 and 15 include analogous recitations. In other words, the claims are directed to extracting vital sign information from a received image of a monitor that is displaying vital
signs information. The claims do not recite generating and displaying vital sign information from processing sensor data, which is nevertheless what the cited references are directed towards.

In rejecting claim 1, the Office references Wang at paragraphs [0004] and [0034] as teaching the "evaluating at least one region of interest of said image [depicting a display screen of a patient monitoring system] comprising one of said vital signs data values to extract said one vital signs data value from said image" as recited by the claims. Office Action,p. 4. Wang neither discloses at least this element, nor has the Office provided any reasoning to support deriving such a teaching from the disclosure of Wang. Rather, Wang discloses, in abstract terms, "'vital sign acquisition cameras' mounted in the waiting room [] configured to periodically perform contactless and/or unobtrusive acquisition of one [or] more updated vital signs and/or physiological parameters from each patient." Wang,par. [0004]. Wang further discloses acquiring vital signs remotely via these "vital sign cameras," but nowhere appears to even contemplate extracting vitals signs from an image of a patient monitoring system display screen, as recited in the claims. Wang, par. [0034].

Beyond the mere mention of similar terms, Wang is not engaging in the same vicinity of solutions, solving the same or similar problems, or applying similar techniques, processes, or systems as the claims. Moreover, neither Banet nor Jacquel cure at least this deficiency of Wang, and so none of Wang, Banet, or Jacquel, either in isolation or taken together, teach each and every element recited by the claims. Accordingly, the claims are patentable over Wang, Banet, and Jacquel. Withdrawal of the rejections and reconsideration is therefore respectfully requested.

While the Applicant believes that the application is currently in condition for allowance, as demonstrated by the above remarks, should the Examiner have any further comments or suggestions, it is respectfully requested that the Examiner telephone the undersigned attorney in order to expeditiously resolve any outstanding issues.
